🚨 'Hello, I'm calling from the Cyber Crime Department. Your Aadhaar is linked to illegal activities.'
Sounds fake?
It isn’t.

Just received a call from 1 such scammer, saying that I had MDMA blah blah.
Brother said that he'll arrest me, I said 'Main Lawrence Bishnoi ki cousin hu'

Thousands of Indians are falling for it every single day.
Bro, who asks money on a whatsapp video call and say 'Arrest kar lenge agr nahi diya toh?'

'Par sir, main toh EMI bhi time pe nahi bhar raha.' 😭

Mere ghar aao agar arrest karna hai, what is this aalas?
And atleast upi sahi karlo - what is inspector1@ptsbi?

Real police don’t use GPay.
They use chappals and FIRs.

Welcome to the hottest thriller of 2024: DIGITAL ARREST SCAM
Genre: Crime | Horror | Tragedy | Comedy (only for the scammers)

How this scam goes -
🎥 A man receives a video call from someone in a police uniform.
📜 There's an FIR in his name.
💰 He’s told to pay ₹2 lakhs “online” to avoid arrest.
🤯 He panics and pays.

Result?
No FIR. No cop. Just a scammer in costume.

📊 FACTS THAT WILL SHOCK YOU
Indians lost ₹120+ CRORE to Digital Arrest Scams between Jan–Apr 2024
Scammers use AI-generated police IDs, fake uniforms, and even deepfake videos to make it real.
Most victims are well-educated professionals who panic in the moment.

💡 If a random person says you're involved in a crime, don’t panic. Pause. Think.
🚔 No real cop asks for UPI payments or WhatsApp calls to avoid arrest.
📱 Block. Report. Stay Safe.

You don’t need a million followers to be impactful.

You just need to be real.

In a world that’s obsessed with being *loud*, I hope you find the courage to be *true*.

Because someone is watching you heal and getting inspired to not give up.
Someone is learning from your calm, your patience, your kindness.
Someone is choosing peace over chaos because of the way you respond to things.
Someone is learning to believe in themselves again because you chose to rise.

You’re doing more than you think.
You’re inspiring people you don’t even know.

So if you ever feel like you’re behind or not doing enough -
remember, growth is not always loud.
Sometimes, it’s silent.
Sometimes, it’s painful.
And most of the time, it’s invisible.

But it’s happening.
And that’s enough.

Keep going.
You’re making a difference just by being *you*.

Let the man cry.

He’s not made of stone.
He’s just been taught to act like one.

From the moment he falls, he’s told -
'Don’t cry like a girl.'
'Be a man.'
'Real men don’t break.'

So, he learns to hide pain.
He smiles when he wants to scream.
He shows strength when he’s drowning.
He says, 'I’m fine' when he’s anything but.

Nobody sees the pressure of being 'the provider,'
The fear of being seen as weak,
The guilt of not doing enough,
The exhaustion of always holding it together.

The world has always given women the space to express.
But men? They cry alone.
In the car.
In the shower.
In silence.

Let the man cry.
Let him breathe.
Let him heal.

Because being a man should never mean suffering in silence.

To every man reading this -
You are allowed to feel.
You are allowed to break.
And you deserve to be heard,
Not just when you're strong,
But especially when you're not.

We raised men to be emotionally homeless.
Where do they go with their pain?

So this is for every man who’s fighting battles he can’t talk about.
Who’s breaking inside, but still shows up for everyone else.
Who’s screaming for help in a world that only listens when he’s successful.

Let the man cry.
Let him fall.
Let him feel.

Because he is not a machine.
He is not your superhero.
He is human.

It’s not unmanly to cry. It’s human.

Rapido drivers never asked for much.
Just a way to earn an honest living.

Karnataka High Court asked Rapido and other bike taxi services to suspend operations until proper guidelines are made.
And honestly, it’s heartbreaking.

Because for us, it’s just news.
For them, it’s their only source of income… gone overnight.

You must’ve met them -
The college student riding in between classes to pay his rent.
The single mom who juggles housework and rides to keep her kids in school.
The man who left his village and came to the city hoping to earn, riding 12 hours a day just to survive.

Most of them don’t have savings.
They don't have backup plans.
They have families to feed, bills to pay, and now… no work.

No one’s saying rules shouldn’t exist.
But can we at least create guidelines without taking away someone’s rozi-roti?

These are not just riders.
They’re people trying to do the right thing - earn money without begging, stealing, or depending on anyone.

I hope the government moves fast.
Because for many, every day without work is a day without food.

I couldn't bargain.

If you know me, you'll know that I am a pro bargainer.

I once legit got a pair of slippers for INR 50 when the shopkeeper started from INR 500.

I've been on vacation since last few days and as usual I wanted to buy something from the local shops.

I chose some bracelets that cost 500 INR in total and I bargained and got them to 280.

Then I was just wondering and saw aunty beading all of them by hand on the road and it got me.

I asked her, how much time does it take to make one and how much does the material cost.

She was making 1 bracelet in 30 mins and all the things including beads, wires and charms cost her around 20.

The pro bargainer in me, stopped at that time and I decided to pay her more for her efforts and she made a customisable bracelet for me!

This wasn't just a piece of jewelry - it was her time, her effort, her livelihood.

Then I came back to Hyderabad, auto waale bhaiya charging 250 INR for a distance of 4 kms got me again!

And suddenly, the pro bargainer in me resurrected from the dead.

The world is wild. Some people will squeeze every penny out of you just because you're a 'tourist.' And some will spend 30 minutes crafting something beautiful, just to make a bare minimum.

If you're going to overpay someone, let it be the one who truly deserves it.

Because behind every street vendor, every roadside artist, and every small business owner, there’s a story we don’t see. A mother trying to send her child to school. A father saving up for a hospital bill. A young girl dreaming of college.

We bargain without thinking - cutting 20, 50, even 100 rupees - because we can. But for them, that’s the difference between a meal and an empty stomach.

So next time you’re about to haggle, just pause for a moment. Look at the person in front of you.

Some things are worth more than their price tag. Some efforts deserve more than a discount. And sometimes, the best deal isn’t about saving money - but making sure someone else gets to earn theirs.

This Generation Got Played - And No One Talks About It

There was a time when people told us:
✨ Study hard, get a degree, and you’ll have a stable job.
✨ Loyalty to a company will reward you.
✨ If you work hard, life will be easy.

They lied.

Houses? Too expensive. Even if you earn well, good luck affording one.

Salaries? Not keeping up with inflation. Meanwhile, CEOs get 2000% hikes.

Job security? You could be replaced by AI, automation, or the next 'cost-cutting' trend.

Work-life balance? A myth. We answer emails at midnight and feel guilty for taking a break.

Older generations tell us, 'You guys don’t work as hard as we did.'

But they didn’t have:
🚩 Unpaid internships.
🚩 Endless job rejections even with experience.
🚩 14-step interview processes just to be ghosted.
🚩 Overqualification being a problem.
🚩 Side hustles just to afford basic expenses.

We were sold a dream that doesn’t exist anymore.

Yet, we’re told we’re 'too sensitive.' That we just need to 'stop complaining and grind harder.'

But how do you grind when:
📌 Rent is half your paycheck?
📌 Therapy is a luxury?
📌 Every passion turns into a side hustle just to survive?

This generation isn’t 'lazy.'
This generation is exhausted.

We adapt, we hustle, we fight for mental health, we question toxic work cultures, we learn new skills every year just to stay relevant.

And we still get blamed.

It’s not that we’re afraid of hard work.
It’s just that the world has changed - 
And no one prepared us for it.

Have you felt this too?

Excited to share my first full-stack Machine Learning project! 🎉
I just completed my own Grocery Management System, combining Python, Flask, and Machine Learning models — and I’m super proud of how it turned out!
🛒 What does the system do?
This system is designed to make grocery product management smarter and more efficient:
✅ Search & browse grocery products easily
 ✅ Purchase items (with automatic, real-time stock updates)
 ✅ Filter products based on price, category, and popularity
 ✅ Predict future sales using Linear Regression
 ✅ Forecast inventory needs using ARIMA time series model
 ✅ Real-time visualizations with Matplotlib to monitor trends
 ✅ A clean, responsive Flask-based web UI with HTML/CSS/JS for seamless interaction

🔍 ML Models Used:
📈 Linear Regression
 Used to analyze how pricing affects product sales. The model helps estimate expected sales volumes based on current prices, allowing dynamic pricing strategies and smarter decision-making for promotions and stock adjustments.
📊 ARIMA (AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average)
 This model forecasts future inventory levels by analyzing past stock trends. It helps prevent overstocking or understocking by generating a daily prediction of stock requirements, ensuring better inventory planning.
✨ I also added graphical plots that show these predictions in real time, giving the user an intuitive understanding of sales and stock movement over time.

💡 Why this project matters to me:
 This was a big step in combining what I’ve learned about data science, machine learning, and full-stack development — all into one functional, real-world application. Seeing it all come together on a working web app was an incredibly satisfying experience.
🔧 Tech stack: Python, Flask, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Pandas, Scikit-learn, Statsmodels, Matplotlib

This is just the beginning — many more projects are on the way! 🚀
 I’d love your thoughts or feedback on how I can make it even better 🙌
 Let’s connect if you’re also into ML, Python, or full-stack dev!

🚀 Just completed my Machine Learning project on Human Activity Recognition in Smart Homes using Python!🧠🏠
Over the past few days, I’ve built a complete Supervised Learning pipeline from scratch, including:
✅ A synthetic dataset simulating motion sensor data (since the original HAR dataset was unavailable)
✅ End-to-end workflow with:
Data Preprocessing & Cleaning
Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Correlation & Covariance
Feature Selection (SelectKBest)
Dimensionality Reduction using PCA
Regression Models (Linear, Ridge, Lasso)
Classification using XGBoost
Evaluation Metrics (R², MAE, RMSE, Confusion Matrix)
Cross-Validation
Learning Curve Visualizations
Gradient Descent understanding
✅ Built an interactive Streamlit web app for real-time predictions & user interaction 🌐
Although the accuracy isn’t perfect (yet!), it was a great hands-on learning experience with both regression and classification approaches, dealing with synthetic time-series-like data, and understanding the pipeline of real-world ML projects.
🔧 Tools & Libraries: pandas, numpy, matplotlib, seaborn, scikit-learn, xgboost, streamlit
🎯 Key Takeaway: A practical reminder that model accuracy isn't everything — clean data, correct preprocessing, and proper model choice matter more than ever.
Big thanks to everyone who inspired or supported me during this! 🙌

Last year, I developed a nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (nMPC) based local planner for a Differential Drive Mobile Robot (DDMR) within the ROS Noetic navigation stack.

Unlike conventional reactive planners, an nMPC uses a mathematical model (in this case, a kinematic model) to predict future states and optimize them over a defined horizon. This is done by minimizing a cost function while satisfying both soft and hard constraints, such as obstacle distance, velocity bounds, and input limits.
The local planner was implemented entirely in Python, utilizing the CasADi framework for formulating the nonlinear optimization problem. The IPOPT solver (Interior Point Optimizer) was used to solve the problem at runtime efficiently.

As part of the evaluation, I compared the nMPC planner against established ROS local planners:
- Dynamic Window Approach (DWA)
- Timed Elastic Band (TEB)
The nMPC planner receives a global reference trajectory (e.g., from an RRT-based global planner) and computes optimized control inputs at higher frequency to achieve smooth and safe local obstacle avoidance, even in dynamic and narrow environments.

- The system was simulated in Gazebo with a TurtleBot platform and fully integrated with ROS Noetic.
- 🐳 A GPU-enabled Docker container is provided for fast and reproducible setup.
- 📁 The GitHub repository includes the full source code, parameter tuning, scientific paper, and presentation slides.
